Sins Of The Demon RPG, developed by Chandler Rounsley and published by Senpai Industrial Studios, is a traditional RPG Maker-style title that leans heavily into familiar genre conventions while managing to distinguish itself through tone, pacing, and a quietly engaging narrative. On the surface, it resembles many other indie JRPG-inspired projects, with its pixel art presentation and turn-based combat, but it gradually reveals a more thoughtful approach to storytelling and progression that gives it a stronger sense of identity than one might initially expect.

The story centers on Kenshi, a wandering demon hunter navigating a world where human sins manifest as literal demonic threats. Accompanied by an unusual partner—a demon cat seeking redemption and restoration—the journey unfolds across a dark fantasy setting that blends moral undertones with supernatural conflict. While the narrative itself is relatively straightforward, it is delivered with a steady rhythm that allows characters and situations to develop naturally. Dialogue and small story moments add texture to the experience, making the world feel more grounded and giving players a reason to stay invested beyond the basic premise.

Combat follows a classic turn-based structure, with a party system built around skills, resource management, and character progression. The mechanics are easy to grasp, making the game accessible even to those less familiar with the genre, while still offering enough variety to keep encounters engaging. Battles are generally well-paced, though the system can be exploited through grinding, allowing players to become overpowered more easily than intended. This flexibility can either enhance or diminish the experience depending on how players approach it, but it does mean that the challenge level is somewhat inconsistent.

Exploration is handled through a network of interconnected areas rather than a traditional overworld map, which gives the game a more cohesive sense of space. Moving between towns, dungeons, and wilderness regions feels natural, and this structure helps maintain immersion throughout the journey. While the environments are functional and varied, they can occasionally feel sparse, lacking the density or detail that might make them more memorable. Even so, the design supports the pacing well, ensuring that players are rarely left without a clear direction forward.

Additional systems such as crafting, side quests, and collectible elements add layers of engagement beyond the main storyline. Crafting allows players to enhance their equipment and tailor their characters to specific playstyles, while side quests provide small narrative expansions and rewards that flesh out the world. These features are not particularly innovative, but they are integrated effectively, contributing to a more complete and satisfying experience overall.

Visually, the game adheres to the familiar RPG Maker aesthetic, with pixel art environments and character sprites that prioritize clarity and consistency over detail. While it does not stand out in terms of graphical presentation, it maintains a cohesive style that supports the game’s tone. The soundtrack complements the atmosphere well, providing a fitting backdrop for both exploration and combat without drawing undue attention to itself.

There are, however, clear limitations. The reliance on established RPG Maker conventions means that the game can feel derivative, particularly for players who have spent significant time with similar titles. Certain systems lack refinement, and the balance issues related to grinding can reduce the sense of progression and challenge. Additionally, while the story is engaging, it does not reach the complexity or emotional depth of more ambitious RPGs.

Despite these shortcomings, Sins Of The Demon RPG succeeds through its consistency and sincerity. It delivers a focused and cohesive experience that captures the essence of classic role-playing games without overextending its scope. For players who appreciate traditional JRPG mechanics and a straightforward but engaging story, it offers a rewarding journey that stands out within its niche.

The story of this game is really interesting - a world that has been cursed that if they commit any of the seven deadly sins they turn into demons.

The first act is very much building up the team, establishing the areas of the world, and levelling up. The second act is very heavy on character backstory and flashbacks, but with far more lore building. There is more content than I expected in this game, taking me about 9 hours to finish. One thing I like is after certain points in the main quests 'skits' would be available to watch which add more detail to the conversations the party has as they move along. A bit of the dialogue is a little cringe (why is the cat trying to hit on every woman) but for the most part is well written. The story builds well, slowly introducing demons of each of the deadly sins before the climax with the final act. Some of the flashback sequences are rather long but interesting.

The combat is pokemon-style except everyone can attack at the same time. Party members gain abilities for which they need special points for, and have different attack speeds. For the most part however, i just spammed the basic attacks and it worked out. At one point the game did turn into a pork bun making simulator as I kept making them until Kenshi's attacks were in the 600s but it did make the combat part of the game rather pointless as he'd just one-shot every enemy.

Overall it is a really sweet RPG which left me feeling happy on story completion.

An RPG set in a fantasy world full of demons who appeared after a curse. A wandering demon hunter and his talking catpanion are on the case. Feel like monster hunting?

The adventure begins with the rescue of a cart randomly attacked by random demons, rewarded with a healthy meal and friends in the local town. This is the intro to a medium-length story focused mainly on solving the mystery of the curse plaguing the land with demons and why Shinto, the cat, can talk. For a low-priced indie RPG, the plot is somewhat decent. It is split into three chapters, with a single ending teased in the intro. There are some more, or less, predicatable plot twists and optional slice-of-life skits sprinkled between the main scenes. Nothing groundbreaking here, but I enjoyed it more than I expected. 
The main characters, Kenshi and Shinto, and the main antagonist, Isharul, are fairly well developed over time, but the rest of the cast is not so much. The flashbacks presented here serve as useful narrative tools. Considering that there are only four characters on your team, more could be done in this department. 
Other than the main story, multiple silly sidequests are also available. While I enjoy doing disconnected tasks, none of them really added anything to the main narrative or character personalities. Missed opportunity.
The world-building is fine. You'll learn a little bit about most places you visit. However, you won't see many locations, and the maps feel rather bland and compressed. The occasional puzzles pose little challenge and lack creativity, but I've seen worse.

While the main focus of this title is on the storytelling, there is some fighting as well. This is, perhaps, the weakest element of this game. Characters level up slowly; levels offer miniscule stat increases; there is a very limited pool of skills that are devoid of upgrades, etc. The slow leveling comes from the low exp from battles and the high HP of later enemies. Fortunately, there are no random encounters.
The only meaningful way to upgrade character stats is through food items. Here, I want to mention the cooking system. You can cook various dishes using recipes found/bought during your travels. Certain dishes increase the character stats, but this requires grinding to earn enough money to buy ingredients. There is also an option to purchase some of the dishes, but it is way more costly. 

The character art is of the generic variety. Simple anime-style portraits can be found in the menu, and that's about it. No CGs or animations. Low-budget game after all.

Music, similarly to art, is also of the generic RPG Maker type. I've heard most of the tracks in other titles already, so there's really nothing to write about. Apt enough track choices serve as background elements.

No bugs encountered.

Overall, a fairly decent story-focused RPG. Unfortunately, the fighting and exploring elements lack creativity and feel like an afterthought. Stil, for a budget title, it is decent enough to earn my approval: 6.4/10

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

Продукты (на 2 порции)
Лаваш тонкий – 1 шт.
Куриная грудка – 300 г
Капуста белокочанная – 200 г
Майонез - 100 г
Огурец свежий – 1 шт.
Помидор – 1 шт.
Лук репчатый красный – 1 шт.
Перец болгарский – 0,5 шт.
Уксус винный белый – 4 ст. ложки
Масло растительное – 4 ст. ложки
Сахар – 1 ч. ложка
Петрушка свежая – 3 веточки
Чеснок – 2-3 зубчика
Соль – по вкусу
Перец черный молотый – по вкусу

В миску выкладываем майонез.
Петрушку промываем, обсушиваем и мелко рубим. Добавляем петрушку в майонез. Очищаем чеснок, пропускаем зубки через пресс. Чесночную массу добавляем в майонез с зеленью. Немного приправляем солью и черным молотым перцем.

Хорошо перемешиваем майонез с чесноком и петрушкой. Соус для шаурмы готов, отставляем его в сторону.

Красный репчатый лук очищаем, нарезаем тонкими полукольцами.

Лук перекладываем в отдельную миску и заливаем винным уксусом. Посыпаем сахаром и щепоткой соли, перемешиваем. Оставляем лук мариноваться.

Куриную грудку нарезаем небольшими кубиками.

В сковороде разогреваем растительное масло. Выкладываем в масло кусочки курицы, сдабриваем их чуть-чуть солью и молотым перчиком. Поджариваем курицу до готовности (около 7-10 минут), периодически помешивая.

Свежий огурчик и сладкий болгарский перец, очищенный от семян, нарезаем соломкой.

Капусту шинкуем. Помидор нарезаем полукружиями. Капусту слегка солим и приминаем руками.
Тонкий лаваш разрезаем на две части (с каждой частью работаем поочерёдно). Подготовленные ингредиенты начинки также делим пополам.
Выкладываем лаваш на стол, одну сторону смазываем майонезным соусом (примерно 2 ст. ложки).

На соус выкладываем капусту.
Замаринованный красный лук освобождаем от маринада, выкладываем на капусту.

Затем распределяем поджаренные кусочки куриной грудки.

На грудку выкладываем измельченный огурец и перец.

Добавляем столовую ложку соуса.
Завершающий слой – нарезанный помидор.

Sins Of The Demon RPG may be a cheap generic RPG Maker title, however that doesn’t mean it is a bad game.
The combat I felt was the weakest part. There’s no equipment, skills are limited, and there’s a lack of enemy variety. It even uses an active time system, but here it feels like a novelty. Midway you can also farm money easily and increase your attack to basically one-hit kill everything if you want. You don’t have to, but otherwise tougher fights will always rely on the same strategies, because your options are limited.
The world map is small, but it’s good enough. You have some places to explore and can even collect some maps that you have to figure out where the loot is. On the plus side, there’re no random encounters. But overall, exploration is nothing special. 
The big focus of the game is the story. It quickly introduces the world and what’s happening, and I immediately got interested by its premise. The first hours are mostly about exploring the world and meeting people, but after that the story ramps-up, with twists and revelations, including some long flashbacks as well. A lot of thought was put into the story, and you can see it. It’s one of the best I’ve seen in these cheap RPG Maker games.
So, if you’re looking for a decent combat and exploration on the cheap, this game isn’t for you. But if you’re looking for an interesting and surprisingly good story, this is definitely worth the price.
